key_insight: Adding more compositional gradient layers in plasma-sprayed La₂Zr₂O₇/NiCoCrAlY thermal barrier coatings smooths the ceramic-to-metal transition, reducing stress concentration and improving high-temperature durability.
engineering_relevance: Multilayer gradient design is a practical route to extend the service life of thermal barrier coatings in turbines and other extreme-temperature components.
method: Compared double-layer, three-layer, and five-layer LZO/NAY gradient architectures.
Characterized microstructure with SEM, EBSD, and TEM.
Used finite element modeling plus thermal shock and oxidation testing to assess stress and durability.
evidence_signal: The five-layer coating showed the most uniform stress distribution, survived 24 thermal shock cycles at 1200 °C versus 18 and 3 for three-layer and double-layer systems, and formed thinner oxide scales after 1000 °C oxidation.
watch_item: The benefit depends on precise layer control and process repeatability, so scaling multilayer gradients may increase fabrication complexity and cost.
paper_title: Multilayer Gradient Design for Stress Mitigation and Durability Enhancement in Plasma-Sprayed La₂Zr₂O₇/NiCoCrAlY Coatings
